videos.title: EXCLUSIVE: Mr. Eazi On Saving Afrobeats, Chop Life Empire & Why Talent Is Not Enough
videos.headline: EXCLUSIVE: Mr. Eazi On Saving Afrobeats, Chop Life Empire & Why Talent Is Not Enough
videos.description:
Mr. Eazi is not holding back. In this exclusive interview on the Midday show with Abi, he makes a bold claim. "I saved Afrobeats in 2016." He talks about the state of the genre back then and how he stepped in to give the people something. But now he is back and he is doing it one more time for the culture. "10 year anniversary. Give thanks to God."

He also opens up about his business ventures. Empower is transitioning into Chop Life, his Disney that wraps up all his entertainment businesses. He speaks on signing new artists like Mr. Eazi and the success they are seeing. "Mr. Eazi put out the first single in October. Smash!" He also talks about Locker Room Bonus, his initiative to build data infrastructure for sports in Nigeria. "It is not CSR. It is selfish. If you want to put money into sport, the data has to be there." Division 2 League players get paid straight to their locker room. No FA. No club. Straight to them.

The conversation also touches on the music. He speaks on his collaboration with Moliy for the song Molly. "She is one of the most talented artists period." He reveals how the song came together, from the sample to the flight from Accra to London. He also talks about his legacy. The Evil Genius album. Accra to Lagos. Lagos to London. And why he had to step back and let his brothers shine. "Let your brother shine." The great philosopher Shea Vibes said it. And Mr. Eazi lived it.

videos.headline: BBNaija Winner Speaks - Luck, Hate, Love and Life After The House | Full Interview at The Beat FM
videos.description:
In this exclusive exit interview, the BBNaija Season 11 finalists and evictees sit down to share their unfiltered truths about life inside the house and what happened after. Temi Nkem, the winner, opens up about being a gambit, feeling like the luckiest man, and why being emotional was never a weakness but a strength. She also addresses the disconnect between her UK accent and the core fan base, explaining that being Nigerian enough has nothing to do with how she speaks. The conversation then shifts to Sheba, who reflects on being the first female Head of House, dealing with age stereotypes, and the real root of her clashes with Tram: ideologies and the way we perceive things.

The housemates take turns revealing their next moves. Aikou talks about turning his imagination into books and music, while Barry shares his plans in fashion, punditry, and acting. Bluethopia gets candid about being misunderstood, her emotional strength, and her upcoming fashion brand. Ricky explains why he deliberately stirred chaos in the house and addresses the flirting with Sheba. Flora speaks on the difficulty of being a gambit and her beauty business goals. Oyin clears up misconceptions about performing for the cameras and reveals her jewelry and modeling plans. Tram discusses coming fifth, feeling appreciated, and his ambition to take over streaming globally. Temi Nkem also talks about driving in Nigeria, going back to school, and becoming a vlogger.

The interview wraps with Sheba explaining that her arguments with Tram were never about the surface issues but about deeper principles. Aikou shares his Abuja roots, Kogi heritage, and his vision for nationalism and Pan-African unity. This is a must-watch for every BBNaija fan who wants to know what really happened inside the Season 11 house and what these stars are planning next.

In this exclusive Cool FM interview and live unplugged performance, the legendary Nigerian rapper, songwriter, and lyricist (known for his deep, reflective style) breaks down the inspiration behind “Dad & Dot,” released in support of the International Day of the Girl Child.

videos.title: Yemi Alade Opens Up: Self-Titled Album, Beauty Line & Why She Named The Project After Herself
videos.headline: Yemi Alade Opens Up: Self-Titled Album, Beauty Line & Why She Named The Project After Herself
videos.description:
Yemi Alade is a force and she is not slowing down. In this exclusive interview on the Midday show with Abi, she opens up about her self-titled album, her beauty line YEM Beauty and why she has always stayed true to herself. She talks about working with Don Jazzy on the video and how she could not keep a straight face. "My face was not straight. I laughed from beginning to end. Don Jazzy himself is such an epitome of blessing. He is so funny."

She also speaks on the new generation of female artists. Tyla, Fave, Tiwa and more. "The females have always just been waiting for this opportunity. And I fear that we are coming in." She gives credit to platforms like OC that share the music of females. "We need more of that in the media space where females are given the opportunity to share their music just because they are musicians, not because of their gender."

The conversation also touches on her album. Titanium is a mashup of R&B, highlife and disco. "I did not spare my vocals." She dreams of having Bruno Mars on it. "I feel like the energies would be so in sync." She also talks about her love for French Africa and France. "I go where the love is." And she reveals that she put out the album title to her fans. "I did not name this album. I put it out to the audience. And the name that kept reoccurring was a self-titled album. It's like a little love note to the fans."

videos.title: Hollywood Meets Nollywood! Djimon Hounsou, Meagan Good, Jonathan Majors, Rita Dominic at AFRIFF 2026
videos.headline: Hollywood Meets Nollywood! Djimon Hounsou, Meagan Good, Jonathan Majors, Rita Dominic at AFRIFF 2026
videos.description:
The 15th edition of the Africa International Film Festival (AFRIFF) is officially underway in Lagos, bringing together some of the biggest names in African and international cinema.

From Nollywood stars Rita Dominic, Osas Ighodaro, and Wale Ojo to international actor and guest of honour Djimon Hounsou, the opening gala was a gathering of filmmakers, actors, and creatives celebrating African storytelling.

With appearances from Meagan Good, Jonathan Majors, Juliet Ibrahim, Toni Tones, Darey Alade, Ruggedman, and many more, the evening set the tone for a week of film, creativity, and industry conversations.

Under the theme “Frames of the Future: Africa’s Creative Intelligence,” AFRIFF 2026 celebrates the evolution of African cinema and its growing influence on the global stage.

We caught up with some of the personalities in attendance to hear their thoughts on African cinema, its future, and the stories taking Africa to the world.

Watch the highlights from the AFRIFF 15th Anniversary Opening Gala.

videos.description:
What happens when one of hip-hop's most elusive albums becomes the subject of a Netflix documentary? RZA, the visionary producer, filmmaker, and founding architect of the Wu-Tang Clan, joins Donwill to discuss The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable, the new documentary chronicling the extraordinary journey of Once Upon a Time in Shaolin. Created as a single-copy work of art, the album became a multimillion-dollar cultural controversy after its sale to Martin Shkreli, raising questions about artistic ownership, creative freedom, and the value of music in the streaming era. RZA reflects on his relationship with producer Cilvaringz, the persistence that brought him into Wu-Tang's orbit, and the philosophical lessons behind a project whose legacy continues to evolve beyond its creators. The RZA breaks down:

- The story behind Once Upon a Time in Shaolin: Why Wu-Tang created a one-of-a-kind album, the controversy surrounding Martin Shkreli, and the project's continuing legacy.
- Cilvaringz and the philosophy of persistence: How an ambitious young artist earned RZA's attention through preparation, determination, and a willingness to learn.
- Artistic ownership in the streaming era: Why scarcity, direct-to-consumer relationships, and devoted fans can change how independent musicians value their work.
- The Wu-Tang business philosophy: Wu Wear, and the group's extended creative universe helped generate opportunities beyond record sales.
- From Prince Rakeem to filmmaker: RZA's experiences with John Woo, Quentin Tarantino, and other filmmakers shaped his creative evolution and ambitions in cinema.

videos.title: Fola Interview: Football Dreams, Davido/ Drake Dream Collab & Why He Believes Anything Is Possible
videos.headline: Fola Interview: Football Dreams, Davido/ Drake Dream Collab & Why He Believes Anything Is Possible
videos.description:
Fola is not your typical lover boy and he is setting the record straight. In this exclusive interview on the Midday show with Abi, he opens up about his new album, his approach to love songs and why he does not rush things anymore. "I know how to narrate love stories very well," he says. "I'm not much that deep of a lover boy like that."

He talks about his song My Type and how it is really a body positivity anthem. "Whatever sort of body type you have, you're beautiful just the way you are." He also speaks on his brotherhood with BNXN and whether an EP together is possible. "BNXN is my brother. Shout out to BNXN." He even reveals that he used to play football actively until he broke his arm. Would he have been a richer footballer than an artist? "I know how to sing more than I know how to play football."

The conversation gets deep when he talks about success and faith. "You can't tell me that nothing is impossible. That's just what I know." He believes Nigerians limit themselves and it is his responsibility to show people that anything can happen. He also reveals he would love a Fola and Drake song and has even written something for it. "When your dreams are too big, they laugh at you."

He also breaks down how 2am in Toronto came together. He recorded it a while ago, stumbled upon it in his archives while on tour in Canada, and reached out to OBO Baddest who picked it and sent it back the same night. The rest is history.

His time at @Interswitch kept his desire to build something that would grow, make an impact, and generate revenue alive. That ambition eventually led him to his co-founder, Felix Ike. Together, they set out to build a company that started as TeamApt and eventually evolved into Moniepoint, one of Nigeria's few unicorns.

Now, the next phase for @moniepointmfb  is about driving that impact across the world.
On this episode of Overnight Success: University Tour Edition, Tosin Eniolorunda takes us through his journey from Ibadan to building a unicorn.

videos.title: Saul Williams on Leap Life, the Politics of Art & the Power of Poetry | The Almanac of Rap
videos.headline: Saul Williams on Leap Life, the Politics of Art & the Power of Poetry | The Almanac of Rap
videos.description:
What happens when an artist refuses to separate creativity from revolution? Poet, musician, actor, filmmaker, and cultural provocateur Saul Williams joins Donwill for an expansive conversation about Leap Life, his first solo studio album in seven years, and Songs My Mother Taught Me, a new nonfiction book examining the experiences and ideas that shaped his political consciousness. 

Working alongside producer Carlos Niño, Williams transforms experimental soundscapes, dance rhythms, and ancestral memory into music that confronts artificial intelligence, colonialism, and the machinery of modern power. From recording a track inside Cairo's bustling streets on his leap-day birthday to hosting listening séances honoring the lives lost to violence, Williams reveals why his latest work is both deeply personal and unapologetically political.

Saul travels with Donwill back to the Brooklyn poetry scene of the 1990s, where Williams shared open-mic stages with future cultural luminaries, including Yasiin Bey and Erykah Badu, before becoming a defining voice of the spoken-word movement. Saul breaks down:

- The making of Leap Life: How Carlos Niño helped transform years of experimental demos into a cohesive album.
- The ideas behind Songs My Mother Taught Me, the influence of Paul Robeson and W.E.B. Du Bois, and why Williams believes music should challenge power rather than reinforce it.
- His first performance at Brooklyn Moon Cafe in 1995, friendships with Yasiin Bey and Erykah Badu, and the creative community that helped bring spoken-word poetry to a new generation.
- His journey through film, theater, and experimental storytelling, including Holler If Ya Hear Me, his years in Paris, and the patience required to create work that defies categorization.
- The relationship between AI and forced labor explored in "Robot Slave," his listening séances, and why fiction, poetry, and music remain essential tools for imagining liberation.
